newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar hits 8-1/2 yr highs despite politics.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar hits 8-1/2 yr highs despite politics.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar powered to fresh 8-1/2 year highs on Friday with a flagrant disregard for politicians intent on forcing it lower.
The currency surged to US$0.7172 in late morning trade, its highest level since mid-1988.

"Fundamentally it's overvalued, but until we get a resolution in the political situation or an easing in monetary conditions, we're not going to see the Kiwi coming off terribly far," said Phil Lindberg, dealer at Bankers Trust.

The Kiwi has hit new 8-1/2 year highs on each of the past three days despite signs that political parties, huddled in closed-door negotiations since inconclusive elections last month, are close to forming a coalition government.
Underpinning the Kiwi are some of the highest real interest rates in the world -- around 7.0 percent.
To take advantage of those rates a succession of eurokiwi and dual currency samurai bonds have been issued -- over NZ$5 billion (US$3.5 billion) this year.
The nationalist New Zealand First Party holds the balance of power and could coalesce with either the caretaker National Party government or the centre-left Labour Party.

NZ First campaigned on an "export-led recovery" and is likely to insist on measures to temper the Kiwi's flight as part of any deal it strikes. But dealers said New Zealand's high real interest rates were simply too attractive to offshore investors.
"You've got to stick with it until we get a resolution in the political situation, until we find out what sort of policies they (the new government) are going to adopt," Lindberg said.
"You really can't do anything else -- you're going to get carved up by being short because of the cost of high interest rates. That's what's really driving it."

By mid-afternoon the Kiwi had settled at 0.7150/57 and 67.06 on its Trade-Weighted Index, but dealers said a retest of its highs and perhaps a look at 72 U.S. cents was definitely on the cards with a steady stream of interbank and customer business.
Technical analysts said the currency looked capable of testing higher still, with ANZ's Mark Elliott saying 0.7225 was the target area.
